auto.text: At the championship the robot ran what the team calls a 4.5 coral auto, a few times reaching 4.83: four coral plus a coral and an algae pickup. The team calls it extremely consistent in qualification, but it scored one coral over all playoffs, after camera disconnects and a reef the team thinks had shifted.

cycle.text: The operator selects things like L1 and L4; position on the field and sensors also decide what the robot does. In a super cycle it picks up algae, scores the coral it already holds in one motion, then scores the algae.

endgame.text: A redesigned climber holds with a servo-engaged ratchet, added because the robot sometimes disengaged while climbing.

gave_up.text: The robot was about 115 lb at its first event and the ground intake added about 16 lb, so that much had to come off elsewhere.
A post that reads as the team's says there was no time to make many spare intake parts before Midwest; plates and tubes slowly broke and the intake broke in finals 2.

changed.text: The first event's robot took coral only from the human player station, which suffered in teleop under defense; a ground intake came before Midwest. The climber was redesigned, and algae gripper compression reduced because algae fell out.
At the championship a borrowed intake roller got four bolts and glue after rollers pulled out of their prints, and it lasted the event; belt tension was raised.

outcome.text: 39-7-0 in official play; ranked 20 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 98.26, Johnson).

functions.name: Ground intake

solves.text: Stop depending on lining up with the human player station under defense

functions.type: ground intake with floating roller and polycarbonate centering

facts.text: A floating roller lets in coral lying perpendicular to the intake
A bottom roller, instead of just a pad, lifts perpendicular coral
A polycarbonate centering piece replaces centering wheels
Two motors: one set of rollers forward and the other backward keeps a coral in the middle, ready for L1

cost.text: A post that reads as the team's says it broke a lot at Midwest, mostly from sideswipes; raising the intake when unused mostly avoids them but is not always possible

The same post says bearing retainer prints tore out until bolts with washers held them, belts jumped off small pulley flanges, and the floating roller's hardstop bolt should sit in a slot so the roller is hard to dislodge
At Midwest, the championship and in practice, rollers sometimes pulled out of their prints because the bolt sits 1/4 in from the tube end
The bottom belt walked off in one match; a bent part added against it got the robot stuck on the reef after L1 a few times, so it was removed and belt tension raised

solves.text: Hold coral through an algae pickup and score it in the same motion

facts.text: Rollers inside the gripper give more traction on the coral, which is upside down while algae is picked up
Made of a composite lighter than polycarbonate

functions.name: Algae gripper

solves.text: Keep algae from falling out of the claw, and score it

functions.type: gripper on the other end of the arm

cost.text: At the first event algae often fell out or could not be scored, so compression was reduced

facts.text: Two Vortex motors, an aluminum barrel and Spectra rigging

solves.text: Stop the robot disengaging from the climb

facts.text: A servo engages a ratchet so the climb holds
Lighter composite parts; weight was cut from the first event's climber

functions.name: Covered belly pan

solves.text: Protect the electronics from loose coral

functions.type: electronics on the underside with a polycarbonate piece added

facts.text: If a coral gets stuck on top, lifting the arm a little frees it

solves.text: Always see a tag while scoring on either branch

facts.text: Crossing the cameras keeps a tag in view when scoring the left or right branch

solves.text: Find coral on the floor for a planned four to five piece ground-intake auto

facts.text: Gives a field position for a coral, which the robot drives to in auto
Can switch to tags when not intaking, for three tag cameras

cost.text: A coral hit made it disconnect in practice, until another camera was borrowed; a bad power path did so again in early championship playoffs

decisions.choice: Add a ground intake between events
decisions.because: teleop under defense suffered, and other teams were doing well with ground intakes
decisions.instead_of: loading only from the human player station

decisions.because: no wheels are needed after the intake

decisions.choice: Make the carriage, coral gripper and climber from a lighter composite
decisions.because: the ground intake's weight had to come off elsewhere
the robot can pick up algae and score coral in one fluid motion
decisions.instead_of: picking up the algae, backing away and moving the arm

decisions.because: a tag is always in view on the left or right branch

decisions.choice: Raise belt tension on the bottom roller
decisions.because: a bent guard got the robot stuck on the reef after L1
decisions.instead_of: a bent guard against belt walking
